title: Variable Intel Report
description: Assign target data to variables and print a formatted report.
problemStatement:
Create a script `intel_report.py` that stores the following information in variables:
- target IP (string, e.g., "192.168.1.105")
- port (integer, e.g., 445)
- service (string, e.g., "SMB")
- is_vulnerable (boolean, e.g., True)

Then, using f‑strings, print a report that looks like this:
```
====== Intel Report ======
Target: 192.168.1.105
Port: 445
Service: SMB
Vulnerable: Yes
===========================
```
If `is_vulnerable` is True, show "Yes", else "No". Use a conditional expression inside the f‑string (like `{"Yes" if is_vulnerable else "No"}`). Make the header lines dynamic based on the length of the title.
hints: The header can be made with `"=" * (len("Intel Report") + 10)`
Make sure you use `str()` for concatenation only if not using f‑strings.
expectedOutput: A nicely formatted report with the target details.
solutionCode:
target_ip = "192.168.1.105"
port = 445
service = "SMB"
is_vulnerable = True

title = "Intel Report"
line = "=" * (len(title) + 10)

print(line)
print(f"  {title}  ")
print(line)
print(f"Target: {target_ip}")
print(f"Port: {port}")
print(f"Service: {service}")
print(f"Vulnerable: {'Yes' if is_vulnerable else 'No'}")
print(line)
